about: A passkey's assertion checked against its account's log, trusting nothing else (DK3, aru-126). The log must be the account's asked about (`account`). Then the whole log, in order: each event is the log's account's, its seq is its place (from 0), its prev the hash of the one before (64 zeros first), its hash its own (SHA-256 of body and proof line), its time not before the one before's, its fields fit their lines (an RP may list several sites, space separated, only on a `by backfill <ms>` event), its key's format its alg's (sec1 for -7, raw for -8, spki for -257), its `by` one of passkey, signup, github, device <id>, session, reset, deleted or backfill <ms>, with a proof exactly when it's passkey; a passkey is added only when it isn't live and removed only when it is, with its key. A proof is checked as an assertion below, by a passkey live just before the event, over SHA-256 of the event's body (base64url), except that its origin must be its RP's own (http or https, the RP as host, any port), not one the verifier pins: whether a log holds together never depends on a verifier's configuration. The first event that fails is `chain`, with its index. Then the assertion's passkey must be live at `at`: added by an event at or before `at`, and not removed by one at or before it (`not_live`). Then, in order: clientDataJSON base64url JSON with type, challenge and origin (`client_data`); type webauthn.get (`ceremony`); the challenge exactly (`challenge`); not crossOrigin true, nor a topOrigin other than origin (`framed`); authenticator data base64url of 37 bytes or more (`auth_data`); its first 32 bytes SHA-256 of the passkey's RP, or of one of them (`rp`); the origin one the verifier allows for that RP (`origin`); flags with UP (0x01) and UV (0x04) (`user`); a key that reads (`key`); the signature, over authenticator data then SHA-256 of clientDataJSON: ES256 DER over P-256, Ed25519 strict, RS256 PKCS#1 v1.5 with SHA-256 (`signature`). Base64url may come padded, but its trailing bits must be zero. The client data is read strictly: a field it reads (type, challenge, origin, crossOrigin, topOrigin) twice is `client_data`; other fields are ignored, twice or not. An ES256 signature's DER integers must be minimal and positive. No provider policy: any AAGUID counts. Ed25519 is checked strictly (Rust's verify_strict); WebCrypto may take small-order keys and non-canonical signatures it would refuse, and no case here has one.

input: log, assertion and origins: labels; account: whose log it should be (origins: { rp: [origins] }, the verifier's pinned map); challenge: base64url; at: ms, the verifier's own record of when it arrived
output: { ok: true, added: the seq of the passkey's added event, rp: the RP it was for }, or { ok: false, refused: a code, event: the index, for chain }
